items.body: Register Login Wild Recall Tyler Pitlick By Brennan McClain | at November 19, 2026 4:00 pm The Minnesota Wild announced they recalled forward Tyler Pitlick from the Iowa Wild in the AHL. Minnesota didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move after placing defenseman Olli Määttä on injured reserve earlier this week. Fortunately, Pitlick’s recall doesn’t correlate with a new injury. According to The Athletic’s Joe Smith , forward Yakov Trenin did not travel with the club for their road trip due to personal reasons. Still, Trenin is expected back during the road trip, so Pitlick was recalled in the meantime. It’s already Pitlick’s third call-up of the 2026-27 campaign. After clearing waivers before the season, Pitlick has been recalled two other times to fill in as an injury replacement for Minnesota. At the end of his last recall, the Wild passed Pitlick through waivers a second time. He’s been fairly quiet during his NHL appearances this year. The 35-year-old depth forward has gone scoreless in 12 games for Minnesota this season while averaging 7:39 of ice time per game. With Trenin expected to return soon, Pitlick is unlikely to enter the lineup. Pitlick has understandably performed better in the AHL, but not by much. In six games with Iowa, Pitlick has registered one goal and three points with a +3 rating. He has 10 more games before requiring waivers for another demotion.

items.title: Wild’s Filip Gustavsson assigned to AHL on conditioning stint
items.summary: Filip Gustavsson went 28-15-6 with a .904 SV% and four shutouts in 50 games with the Minnesota Wild in 2025-26.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Minnesota Wild announced Thursday that goaltender Filip Gustavsson has been assigned to their AHL affiliate on a conditioning stint. He is expected to start for the Iowa Wild this Saturday against the San Diego Gulls. Gustavsson, 28, underwent hip surgery in the summer and started the season on injured reserve . In 2025-26, he went 28-15-6 with a .904 save percentage (SV%) and a 1.4 goals saved above expected (GSAx) with four shutouts in 50 games. This season will be the first in a five-year, $34-million contract extension that Gustavsson signed in October 2025. He will carry a cap hit of $6.8 million through the 2030-31 campaign. In six NHL seasons, the Skelleftea, Sweden, native is 111-74-26 with a .911 SV% and a 2.67 goals against average (GAA) in 219 appearances with the Wild and Ottawa Senators . He also has a 4-7 record with a .911 SV% and 2.67 GAA in 12 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. Gustavsson was taken in the second round of the 2016 NHL Entry Draft by the Pittsburgh Penguins . He spent two more seasons developing in Sweden’s top professional hockey league with Lulea HF before he moved to North America. In 2018, Gustavsson was traded to the Senators, along with Ian Cole, a first-round pick and a third-round pick in exchange for Derick Brassard. He spent parts of five seasons with their AHL affiliate, the Belleville Senators, where he posted a 45-39-8 record with an .898 SV% and 3.06 GAA in 95 appearances.

items.body: Register Login Kraken Activate Jacob Melanson; Reassign Jani Nyman By Brennan McClain | at November 19, 2026 3:04 pm According to a team announcement , the Seattle Kraken activated forward Jacob Melanson from the injured reserve. In a corresponding roster move, the Kraken assigned forward Jani Nyman to the Coachella Valley Firebirds in the AHL. Melanson, 23, has missed much of the 2026-27 campaign. First diagnosed with an upper-body injury, further testing revealed that Melanson was suffering from an anterior mediastinum hematoma with a vascular pseudoaneurysm. Essentially a collection of blood behind the chest cavity, it could have ruptured and proved life-threatening had Melanson returned to the ice too quickly. Given the seriousness of the diagnosis, it’s incredibly fortunate news that Melanson could return. He’s appeared in only one contest for the Kraken so far this season. items.body: The goaltender has been assigned to the Minnesota Wld's affiliate, the Iowa Wild, for a conditioning assignment, the team announced Thursday. The expectation is that Gustavsson will start for Iowa in Saturday's game at San Diego. The 28-year-old has not played since May 5, following hip surgery during the off-season. In Gustavsson's absence, Jesper Wallstedt has mainly tended Minnesota's crease with 20 starts, while Calvin Pickard has backed up with 3 starts. Gustavsson was 28-15-6 with a 2.69 goals-against average and .904 save percentage in 50 games (49 starts) last season. He is in the first year of a five-year contract that carries a $6.8 million cap hit. The Wild (16-3-4) enter their game Thursday against the Calgary Flames, sitting first in the Central Division and second in both the Western Conference and the league overall.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Logan Thompson and Charlie Lindgren took the ice with new masks at Thursday’s morning skate — and for a good cause. The special goalie masks were designed in recognition of the NHL’s Hockey Fights Cancer Month and will be worn when the Washington Capitals face off against the Buffalo Sabres for Hockey Fights Cancer Night later this evening. The masks are a part of a Monumental Sports & Entertainment Foundation auction with proceeds benefiting cancer-related causes. Thompson’s mask is especially emotional as it was inspired by 14-year-old William Martel of King William, Virginia, who was diagnosed with brain cancer in December 2025. Martel, who lost vision in his left eye due to a germinoma tumor, first met Thompson in June 2026 while undergoing radiation treatment. Having admired Thompson’s goalie mask, Martel wanted his own radiation treatment mask to look just as “cool” and modeled its design after the Capitals goaltender’s mask. When the two met in June, Thompson and Martel spent time sketching their dream goalie masks together. Their collaboration helped inspire Thompson’s special Hockey Fights Cancer mask, which incorporates several of Martel’s personal interests and hobbies. items.title: Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness set to return from health issue
items.body: Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness is set to resume his post behind the bench after missing three games with an undisclosed health issue. The 71-year-old informed the team of his return for their game against the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday before its road practice the day before. “We’ve missed a week,” Bowness told The Athletic. “That’s a long time, so I’m thrilled to be back. “It’s weird watching the games. It’s a little different. You’d rather be here with the guys. You want to be in the fight. That’s the biggest thing. It’s good to be back in the fight with these guys.” The Blue Jackets lost all three games in Bowness's absence. He stayed in Columbus on Monday to undergo various medical tests when the team first departed on its current four-game road trip. First-year assistant Don Granato took over the team while Bowness was away.

items.title: Report: Simon Edvinsson passed on multiple offer sheets to force exit from Red Wings
items.summary: Edvinsson must sign by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 to be eligible to play in the NHL this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The situation between the Detroit Red Wings and defenseman Simon Edvinsson keeps getting uglier. Edvinsson, 23, is currently a restricted free agent, having not yet signed an extension with the Red Wings following the completion of his three-year, entry-level deal last season. He must sign a deal by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 in order to be eligible to play in the NHL this season. According to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli, Edvinsson has turned down offer sheets from multiple teams in order to deny Detroit the opportunity to match, putting pressure on the Red Wings to simply trade him before the December 1 deadline. “He’d love to be signed and playing,” a source told Seravalli. “But he no longer wants to play in Detroit and that would be the risk with an offer sheet.” Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff mentioned earlier this season that he has “zero interest” in trading Edvinsson. Horcoff may be forced to change his tune, or else risk losing Edvinsson for the season if nothing gets done ahead of the December 1 deadline. Detroit would still retain Edvinsson’s rights in that case, but would presumably receive less appealing trade offers for a player that could no longer play this season. Seravalli also pointed out that there is a daily cap penalty for the first year of a contract given to a restricted free agent after the start of the regular season, meaning the cap hit for this season on any deal Edvinsson may ultimately sign gets higher with each day he remains unsigned. Selected sixth overall by the Red Wings in the 2021 NHL Entry Draft, Edvinsson had nine goals and 16 assists for 25 points in 72 games with Detroit last season, while averaging just under 22 and half minutes of ice time.

items.body: Captain injured during face-off against Maple Leafs on Tuesday CHICAGO -- Connor Bedard will miss at least the next four games for the Chicago Blackhawks, who are deciding if he needs surgery on his right shoulder. "Collectively as a group, I would say we’re still gathering information," coach Jeff Blashill said Thursday, "weighing the different decision process between rehab and surgery. Once those decisions are made, then I’d have more for you after that. "He definitely won’t play tonight and definitely won’t play on the road trip." The Blackhawks (6-13-2) play the Columbus Blue Jackets (7-12-0) at United Center on Thursday (8 p.m. ET; CBJHN, CBJNHL, CHSN), before starting a three-game road trip at the Calgary Flames (Saturday), the Vancouver Canucks (Sunday) and Seattle Kraken (Wednesday). The 21-year-old captain was injured in the Blackhawks’ 6-3 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday. He was set to take a face-off against Maple Leafs forward Nick Paul 54 seconds into the third period when, as Bedard put his stick on the ice, Paul’s stick made contact with Bedard’s right hand. He yelled out in pain and immediately went to the locker room. Bedard leads the Blackhawks with 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games. items.summary: After Tuesday’s embarrassing loss in Chicago, Toronto Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller stated that lineup tweaks were coming. Now that they’re here, Luke Fox breaks down the fallout.

items.summary: In March 2025, the Toronto Maple Leafs pulled off a couple of big moves in quick succession in pursuit of a playoff run, trading away a pair of first-round picks. Two years later, they’re about to pay the price.
items.body: In March 2025, the Toronto Maple Leafs pulled off a couple of big moves in quick succession in pursuit of a playoff run, trading away a pair of first-round picks. Two years later, they’re about to pay the price. Only, it’s a little more complicated than that. And as Toronto finds itself mired in a losing streak, the club’s draft stock skyrocketing as they fall down the league standings, those picks are suddenly in the spotlight once again. While last year’s struggles were met with the king of all consolation prizes in the form of the club landing the No.1 overall pick and the rights to select Gavin McKenna, there will be no such silver lining this season. The Maple Leafs don’t own their 2027 first-round pick — that belongs to Boston. Or is it Philadelphia? Just prior to the 2025 trade deadline, the Maple Leafs dealt two first-round picks in two separate transactions. First, they acquired forward Scott Laughton from the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for a conditional 2027 first-round pick and forward Nikita Grebenkin. (Toronto also got the Flyers’ 2025 fourth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder in the deal.) The Maple Leafs’ departed first-round pick came with the condition that Toronto could push the selection to 2028 in the event it wound up within the top 10. items.body: Register Login Injury Notes: Gadjovich, Moore, Trudeau By Brennan McClain | at November 19, 2026 12:00 pm A few weeks ago, Florida Panthers forward Jonah Gadjovich went a full calendar year without playing an NHL game. Last season, Gadjovich suffered a serious neck injury that required surgery. His initial recovery timeline projected a three-month absence, though multiple setbacks have kept Gadjovich out much longer than expected. Fortunately, the fourth-line forward took a meaningful step forward this morning. According to Florida Hockey Now’s George Richards , Gadjovich returned to the Panthers’ practice in a non-contact jersey. Still, there’s no update on when he’ll return, and it’s likely he’ll need several weeks to ramp up to playing speed. Before the injury, Gadjovich spent three years with the Panthers as a hyperphysical bottom-six forward. From 2023-24 to 2025-26, Gadjovich registered six goals and 11 points in 91 games with a -5 rating, while averaging 7:57 of ice time per game. On the physical side, Gadjovich averaged nearly one minor penalty and 2.5 hits per game.

items.title: Sources: Edvinsson passed on offer sheets to avoid staying in Detroit
items.summary: Sources say Simon Edvinsson has refused offer sheets because he doesn’t want to allow Detroit to match. Frank Seravalli has the latest on the saga.
items.body: Time is up on Simon Edvinsson ’s tenure with the Detroit Red Wings — the only question that remains is whether a trade will be executed prior to Dec. 1’s deadline or cost him the season. While interim GM Shawn Horcoff indicated as recently as last week that his intention was still to sign Edvinsson, that ship has sailed. Sources say multiple teams made overtures on offer sheets in an attempt end the saga but Edvinsson has chosen not to engage because he does not want to give Detroit an opportunity to match. “He’d love to be signed and playing,” one source said. “But he no longer wants to play in Detroit and that would be the risk with an offer sheet.” Ten of the 14 offer sheets signed in the NHL’s salary cap era have been matched by the team holding the restricted free agent, including both Leo Carlsson and Barrett Hayton last summer. The clock is ticking. Horcoff and the Red Wings seem comfortable making the Edvinsson camp sweat by taking it to the deadline, now just 12 days away. Deadlines produce transactions in the NHL but there is considerable risk on both sides in this game of chicken. For Edvinsson, his age-23 season hangs in the balance. A contract for Edvinsson must be registered with the NHL by 5 p.m. ET on Dec. 1 for him to be eligible to play with any team for the remainder of the season. For the Red Wings, it’s entirely possible that the trade return weakens leading up to Dec. 1 as opposed to getting stronger. Opposing teams believe inaction is not an option, that they won’t want to kick the can down the road until next summer. items.title: Blackhawks considering surgery for Connor Bedard
items.summary: Bedard appeared to injure his shoulder during the Blackhawks’ win over the Maple Leafs on Tuesday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Blackhawks are weighing whether or not forward Connor Bedard should undergo surgery for an upper-body injury sustained earlier this week, head coach Jeff Blashill told reporters Thursday. Blashill also confirmed that Bedard wouldn’t play Thursday night against the Columbus Blue Jackets or at all during the Blackhawks’ upcoming three-game road trip. Bedard, 21, suffered the injury during the team’s 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs Tuesday. He appeared to injure his shoulder before a faceoff and went straight off the ice towards to the dressing room. He has seven goals and 11 assists for 18 points in 15 games this season. Now in his fourth NHL campaign, the right-handed center has 82 goals and 139 assists for 221 points in 234 regular-season contests. Bedard was named the 37th captain in Blackhawks history last September. Before that, he signed a five-year, $75-million contract extension that carries an annual cap hit of $15 million. Chicago selected Bedard with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 NHL Entry Draft. In three seasons of junior hockey with the Regina Pats of the Western Hockey League, he scored 134 goals and recorded 137 assists for 271 points in 134 career regular-season games. The North Vancouver, B.C., native has also represented Canada on numerous occasions at the international level. He was part of back-to-back IIHF World Junior Championship gold medal-winning squads in 2022 and 2023. The Blackhawks are 6-13-2 with 14 points through their first 21 games of 2026-27. They are last in the Central Division and carry the second-worst record in the NHL .

Bedard will remain out at least through Chicago's upcoming road trip, Blashill said. Bedard got hurt on a faceoff early in the third period of Tuesday night's 6-3 win over Toronto. The 21-year-old centre slammed his stick on the ice and held his right arm in front of him as he made his way to the locker room. The 2023-24 Rookie of the Year has 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) through 15 games. He became the second-youngest captain in Blackhawks franchise history at the start of the season. Anton Frondell stepped in as Chicago's No. 1 centre in practice on Wednesday, skating on a line with rookie Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The lead-up to the 2027 World Junior Championship in Edmonton and Red Deer has been anything but ordinary. Late last month, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Russia was to be allowed immediately back into international competitions, starting with the World Juniors later this year. That meant Norway was getting pushed out despite earning a spot through the proper qualification process last winter. Then, nearly every single team said they would boycott playing against the Russians, with the Canadian government even outright banning visas to the players. items.body: Register Login Lightning Recall Jansen Harkins By Gabriel Foley | at November 19, 2026 9:50 am The Tampa Bay Lightning have added a forward to the lineup with four games left in their current homestand. Centerman Jansen Harkins has been recalled for the first time this season. Harkins broke camp with Tampa Bay and played in the first game of the season before being reassigned on October 7th. He has since appeared in 11 games with the AHL’s Syracuse Crunch. Harkins has recorded six points and four penalty minutes in those minor-league appearances. Harkins is in his first season in the Lightning organization after spending the last two seasons as a depth forward with the Anaheim Ducks. He spent much of that tenure in the NHL lineup, appearing in 106 games with Anaheim marked by 14 points and 49 penalty minutes. Harkins also appeared in 11 games with the San Diego Gulls where he scored a productive 17 points. His career has winded through depth roles, also taking him through four seasons with the Winnipeg Jets and one year with the Pittsburgh Penguins. Harkins’ call-up will serve as insurance as the team faces injuries to Conor Geekie , Brandon Hagel , and Zemgus Girgensons . Both Hagel and Girgensons are out day-to-day while Geekie was recently placed on injured reserve. Harkins won’t face much competition for a lineup role after Tampa Bay chose to ice 11 forwards and seven defensemen in Tuesday’s win over the Washington Capitals. Should the club want to return to a 12-forward lineup, Harkins’ would have a carved out role at fourth-line center between Jeffrey Viel and Scott Sabourin . Through the partnership, RCX Sports will provide local league operators with the resources, guidance, and programming needed to deliver high-quality, engaging street hockey experiences. items.title: Mammoth beat Avalanche to end six-game slide
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Vincent Trocheck scored a goal and assisted another to help the Utah Mammoth beat the Colorado Avalanche 4-1 on Wednesday night and snap a six-game losing streak. Liam O’Brien, Dmitri Simashev and Kevin Stenlund scored goals for the Mammoth. Sebastian Cossa made 30 stops. Mackenzie Blackwood tallied 25 saves for Colorado. Jaden Schwartz scored the lone goal for the Avalanche. O’Brien put Utah on the board at 5:22 of the second, blasting a one-timer from the faceoff circle for his first goal of the season. Trocheck made it a two-goal lead with a power-play goal with 2:07 left in the second. He slid out to the circle and slapped the puck home off a crisp feed from Keller. Utah went up 3-0 only 62 seconds into the third after Simashev snapped in the puck from the circle for a short-handed goal. Colorado started both the second and third periods with power-play chances but were unable to capitalize. Schwartz’s unassisted goal with 4:59 left helped the Avalanche avoid a shutout. Stenlund capped the scoring on an empty netter with 2:08 remaining.

items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Hours before the Montreal Canadiens bounced back from what Martin St. Louis termed to be “pretty much the worst” game they’d played this season, the coach sung his most common refrain. “All team sports are the same,” St. Louis began. “I didn’t invent these rules of being in space and breaking pressure with being in balance on the ice. When you play inside that, you raise your percentages of having success and you get the bounces. When you don’t do that, your percentages of having success go down and you go looking for bounces. When you do things the right way, you get goals and bounces and a high percentage of success.” That was what he said at his morning media availability. items.title: Senators’ Tyler Boucher to have father Brian Boucher call game vs. Flyers
items.body: Ottawa Senators rookie Tyler Boucher will have a friendly face calling his game for the opposition broadcast on Thursday. His dad, former NHLer Brian Boucher, will be in the booth for NBC Philadelphia's local broadcast when the Philadelphia Flyers visit the Senators on Thursday — a game in which the younger Boucher is expected to play. "I mean, I'm going to try to keep it as normal as possible, treat him like another player, but I am going to be keeping a close eye on him for sure," Brian told NHL.com's Dan Rosen on Wednesday. "I've got to be honest with you, I've dreamt about this moment since he's been drafted. For me personally, I don't know about for him, but since I got into this side of the game I've always been like, 'Man, it would be so cool to call his games.' It would be really meaningful to me. I've never told him that because I've never wanted to put pressure on him, but for me personally it's going to be a special moment and I'm looking forward to it if it does happen." Brian played for the Flyers for six seasons in three separate stints before his retirement following the 2012-13 season. Tyler was selected by the Senators with the 10th-overall pick of the 2021 draft and made his debut on Tuesday night — scoring his first NHL goal in the process. The elder Boucher said that while he doesn't consider himself to be a typical hockey dad, he admitted that it's "better to be upstairs so (Tyler) doesn't see my facial reactions." "So, I'll be upstairs and he won't see my reactions if he makes a boneheaded play or something like that."

items.title: Canadiens end power-play drought in win, hand Hellebuyck 1st Devils loss
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Jake Evans scored the go-ahead goal, captain Nick Suzuki ended his team's long power-play drought and the Montreal Canadiens defeated the New Jersey Devils 3-2 on Wednesday night to halt a two-game skid. Connor Hellebuyck got a piece of Evans' shot with his glove but could not keep it out of the net. The goal with 13:43 left sparked “Go, Habs, go!” chants from the many Canadiens fans in attendance. Hellebuyck allowed three goals on 27 shots and lost for the first time in eight starts since joining New Jersey in a trade from Winnipeg in late October. Despite Timo Meier setting up a goal by Luke Evangelista and scoring on a breakaway fresh out of the penalty box, the Devils had their two-game winning streak snapped, losing for just the second time in their past nine. The Canadiens only trailed for 40 seconds after Evangelista's goal, as Alex Newhook got in on net and made a nifty move to beat Hellebuyck and tie it. After spending time practicing the power play on Tuesday and devoting significant conversation to what was going wrong, they came up empty on their first two chances. With Montreal's run at 0 for its past 14, a parade to the penalty box eventually came back to bite New Jersey. Suzuki drew a tripping penalty on Brenden Dillon, then deflected Lane Hutson's point shot in past Hellebuyck with 41.9 seconds remaining in the first period. Jacob Fowler stopped all 20 shots he faced in the second and third, finishing with 27 saves and avoiding what would have been his first time losing consecutive games this season. He and his teammates successfully killed a penalty in the final minutes to seal it. items.title: Bruins beat Red Wings, spoil Detroit’s Centennial celebration game
items.body: DETROIT — David Pastrnak had a goal and an assist as the Boston Bruins beat Detroit 4-1 on Wednesday night and spoiled the Red Wings' Centennial celebration game. The contest was played on the 100th anniversary of Detroit’s first NHL game — a 2-0 loss for the then-Cougars to the Bruins. Pregame ceremonies on Wednesday included a video introduction from Scotty Bowman. The centennial celebration resulted in a rare color-on-color game, with Detroit wearing red and the Bruins in black. JJ Peterka and Pavel Zacha also scored for the Bruins, who snapped a three-game skid. Mason Lohrei and Morgan Geekie each had two assists. Daniil Tarasov, coming off a shutout of the Tampa Bay Lightning, made 27 saves, but couldn’t prevent Detroit’s sixth loss in seven games. Detroit's Lucas Raymond made it 1-0 at 16:58 of the first period. Keegan Kolesar knocked the puck loose in the neutral zone to set up a 2-on-1 break, and Raymond blasted Andrew Copp’s pass inside the left post for his ninth goal. Peterka tied the game at 2:47 of the second, cutting in from the left wing and beating Tarasov on the glove side. Zacha then gave the Bruins a 2-1 lead with a power-play goal at 11:48, putting in a rebound for his sixth of the season. Pastrnak made it 3-1 at 5:11 of the third, beating Tarasov from the slot after a pass from Lohrei. Casey Middelstadt finished the scoring into an empty net at 19:05.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Maple Leafs, Bolduc, Shepard By Bradley Keith | at November 18, 2026 9:29 pm Unable to end what is now a brutal seven game losing streak after last night’s 6-3 loss to Chicago, the noise only gets louder for the Maple Leafs. David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period reports that President and CEO Keith Pelley traveled with the group for the game and had unpleasant conversations with what the insider called “key personnel” on the team. Not confirming exactly who it may have been, one can assume new head coach Jim Hiller ’s rough start to his tenure was a key part of any conversation. Even if the near-sighted decisions by John Chayka to make large commitments to an aging Sergei Bobrovsky , a late-blooming Darren Raddysh , and bottom-sixers like Colton Sissons would bite them sometime later, the expectation was at least to buy another 2-3 year window and figure out the rest in the future. Instead we’re not even in December and there’s already questions being raised . Toronto is 1-9-0 in their last 10, 27th in the NHL. Their offensive production has been acceptable, but it’s their other classic shortcomings which continue to hamper the group. Nearly two years ago today the Blues fired Drew Bannister 22 games into their season, although the coach had 76 total games behind the bench before the decision was made, counting the season prior. items.body: Former goalie will broadcast forward’s next game against Flyers on Thursday The 49-year-old former NHL goalie has spent his entire life in the game, more than half of it in the League as either a player or broadcaster, but never before did he experience what he felt while in the stands at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg alongside his wife, Melissa, and daughter, Brianna, watching his son, Tyler, score the game-winning goal in his NHL debut with the Ottawa Senators. "I mean, I've had some cool moments in my career; five shutouts in a row stands out," said Boucher, who set the NHL record for longest shutout streak (332:01) in 2003-04. "Win an eight-period game in Pittsburgh in the playoffs, five overtimes (in 2000). But this is better just because it's your kid, and we're all so proud of our children." "I think what I'm most proud of with him, honestly, it's not that he played his first NHL game or that he scored, that's awesome stuff, but it's the story behind it and the resilience and perseverance and fight that he showed," Brian Boucher said. items.summary: It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud.
items.body: CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Pa. — It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud. Asked Wednesday what gives him hope that his struggling team, which is mired near the bottom of the Eastern Conference and has three regulation wins through 20 games, can turn it around in time to salvage this season, Dubas turned philosophical. Yes, making the playoffs for a second straight year would be nice. Yet that's not the metric he will lean on to gauge progress. Dubas would like the team's younger players to take “major steps.” He'd like to see the iconic, aging core led by captain Sidney Crosby show it still has “gas left in the tank." He'd like some of the prospects he's acquired since taking over to make a push for NHL playing time. If those things can happen, Dubas believes the franchise will be on “the right track" regardless of where the Penguins wind up in the standings. Then, Dubas finished by using a phrase that included the one word he has consistently avoided uttering publicly since taking over in the summer of 2023. “This has been, I think rightfully, an unorthodox style of rebuilding a team because of the players that are here,” he said. If Mitchell clears waivers on Thursday, he’ll become eligible to be assigned to the Ducks’ American Hockey League affiliate, the San Diego Gulls. Mitchell has actually seen some considerable time with the Ducks in the first two months of the 2026-27 season. items.body: Teammates 'watching greatness kind of evolve' in 19-year-old defenseman ELMONT, N.Y. -- Matthew Schaefer 's eyes, along with those of his New York Islanders teammates, grew about as wide as the concourses at UBS Arena with 4:25 remaining in the third period Tuesday, up by three goals and the Columbus Blue Jackets opting to pull their goaltender. The defenseman already had scored twice and was presented a sixth opportunity to achieve one of the few things that he had been denied despite being only 100 games into his NHL career and having turned 19 two months ago. "I was out there and I didn't know if they were (going to pull Cam Talbot) or not, and I see them pull him and I’m like, 'Oh!'" Schaefer said. "They got to do what they got to do. "We were just focused on the game and if it happened, it happened. If it didn't, it's not the end of the world. We just want to win in here." Schaefer no longer has to wait. He completed his first NHL hat trick at 16:08 of the third in a 5-1 victory, becoming the first Islanders defenseman to accomplish the feat since Denis Potvin on March 4, 1982. "It might've been a little too hard of a celly," Schaefer said. "Maybe I should have been a little more respectful with it, but it's awesome. Anytime something like that happens … it's pretty cool, but it was just a big win in general overall with a great team effort." items.title: ‘Don’t fall’: NHLers look back on their rookie initiation laps
items.body: The Maple Leafs rookie selected No. 1 overall at the 2026 draft stepped on the ice for his solo lap at the start of warm-ups — a playful, often helmetless indoctrination for players set to make their debuts — in late September. Toronto goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky was so in the zone ahead of the season-opener that he mistakenly joined the 18-year-old before later apologizing for the gaffe. McKenna wasn't fussed. Like every other youngster taking that solitary twirl, he was living out a childhood dream. "Hard to forget a day like this," the peach-fuzzed winger said. "All pretty special." The league's rookie lap is a relatively new tradition, one started organically when veterans began hiding helmets ahead of first games — a prank that became ingrained in most teams' culture — before the rest of the roster joins warm-ups after a few dozen lonely strides around the rink. Logan Cooley came out of the tunnel on his own as a member of the Arizona Coyotes in New Jersey back in 2023. "I wish in the moment I could have enjoyed it a lot more," said Cooley, now a forward with the Utah Mammoth following the franchise's relocation. "There's a lot of excitement, a lot of nerves, a ton of family in the arena. It didn't really feel real." New York Islanders defenceman Matthew Schaefer received some brotherly grief for not being ready for his rookie lap last season in Pittsburgh. "I was rushing out there and then my hair was down in my eyes, and he's like, 'You're not going to put some gel in?'" Schaefer said. "You're like, 'Wow, this is the NHL.' Your helmet's off, you're flying around … you're thinking, 'Please don't eat it.'" Dallas Stars centre Wyatt Johnston , much like Schaefer, just wanted to avoid embarrassment in Nashville. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The San Jose Sea Lions are adjusting their goaltending setup as training camps open for the club’s first-ever PWHL season. In her place, Abstreiter steps in, also bringing three years of PWHL experience. items.title: NHL Unveils 2026 Winter Classic Jerseys For Utah Mammoth And Colorado Avalanche
items.summary: Mammoth and Avalanche will square off in outdoor game on New Year's Eve in Salt Lake City.
items.body: Photo: NHL Photo: NHL NHL Unveils 2026 Winter Classic Jerseys For Utah Mammoth And Colorado Avalanche Eric Cruikshank Partner Nov 18, 2026 4:24 PM Published Nov 18, 2026 4:24 PM Mammoth and Avalanche will square off in outdoor game on New Year's Eve in Salt Lake City. The Colorado Avalanche and Utah Mammoth have some new threads for their upcoming outdoor battle. The NHL and Fanatics released the two sets of uniforms to be worn for Winter Classic, which will be played on New Year's Eve at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. The Avalanche jersey takes on a cream-colored base with a deep burgundy and dark blue scheme, featuring a vintage 'C' logo on the jest with a mountain range inside the signage. The gloves and pants will also carry the same maroon color while the socks will maintain the dark blue and cream colors. The Mammoth will boast a bright-blue based jersey, similar to the color of the franchise's recently released Hometown Remix sweater . Like the Avalanche, the Mammoth will also have a cream secondary color with a striped pattern on the sleeves of the arms. The center crest features the city plated across the chest with a brown mammoth logo underneath the text. The Mammoth will also have bright blue helmets and will wear brown on the gloves and pants. This will be the 47th regular-season outdoor game the NHL has hosted, and it will be the first time the Mammoth have competed in one. This will be the third time the Avalanche have appeared in an outdoor game, having suited up for the 2016 Stadium Series against the Detroit Red Wings , the 2020 Stadium Series against the Los Angeles Kings , and the 2021 Lake Tahoe game against the Vegas Golden Knights .

items.title: Boston College to retire Johnny Gaudreau’s No. 13
items.summary: The late Johnny Gaudreau had 175 points in his collegiate career with Boston College and won the Hobey Baker Award in 2014.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Johnny Gaudreau at Boston College The Boston College Eagles men’s hockey program announced on Wednesday that it will retire the iconic No. 13 jersey once worn by the late Johnny Gaudreau on Feb. 12, 2027. Gaudreau, who spent the 2011-12 through 2013-14 seasons in Chestnut Hill before beginning his NHL career, is one of the most decorated players in the storied program’s history. He produced 175 points in 119 career games, helped lead the program to the national championship in 2012, and won the Hobey Baker Memorial Award as collegiate hockey’s top player in 2014. “We are proud to honor Johnny Gaudreau by retiring his No. 13 at Boston College,” Boston College athletic director Blake James said via the school’s press release. “Johnny was an extraordinary player who helped bring a national championship to the Heights and became one of the most accomplished players in our program’s history. He will always hold a special place in the Boston College family.” Gaudreau, along with his younger brother and fellow Boston College alum Matthew, passed away in August of 2024 when they were struck and killed by a motor vehicle while riding bikes near their hometown of Carneys Point, New Jersey. Boston College was where Gaudreau earned the moniker “Johnny Hockey” and established himself as a slam-dunk future star before going on to have a prolific NHL career with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets . Since his passing, extensive tributes to recognize his profound impact on the sport have poured in from not only Boston College, but also the Flames, Blue Jackets and USA Hockey. items.body: Designs for Avalanche, Mammoth inspired by outdoor hockey, alpine nostalgia NEW YORK – Today, the National Hockey League (NHL) and Fanatics, the authentic outfitter of the NHL, unveiled uniforms for the Discover NHL Winter Classic, to be worn when the Utah Mammoth host the Colorado Avalanche on New Year’s Eve at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. The marquee matchup will be the first NHL outdoor game played in Utah, to take place during the team’s third season, and the Utah Mammoth’s first-ever outdoor appearance. As the newest club in the league, Utah will be the 32nd NHL franchise to compete in a regular-season outdoor game. The NHL Winter Classic in Utah will mark the 47 th NHL regular-season outdoor game. Designed by Fanatics in collaboration with both clubs and the League, the uniforms are inspired by outdoor hockey played at the base of ski hills and alpine nostalgia, where the sport naturally connects with mountain communities and winter traditions. Drawing on the hockey history of each state and the ski culture Utah and Colorado share, both designs bring the spirit of mountain hockey to the first NHL outdoor game in Utah. Rooted in the history of hockey in the state, the Utah Mammoth will sport a Mountain Blue jersey with brown and beige detailing that brings a vintage look and pays homage to the fur of a woolly mammoth. A throwback-inspired rendering of the club’s walking mammoth logo anchors the crest, while on the helmet, a tusk forms the crossbar of the “T” in “Utah.” The design inspiration behind Utah’s NHL Winter Classic jersey draws from early days of community hockey in the state. items.summary: Amid a 7-11-6 start, the Philadelphia coach’s problems go deeper than the Michkov relationship.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images Six short months ago, the Philadelphia Flyers ’ long-tormented fanbase enjoyed a run of good fortune unlike any it had in the previous decade. The furious post-Olympics heater that dragged the Orange and Black off the deck and into the playoff hunt. The brilliant late-season debut of collegiate star Porter Martone. Tyson Foerster’s shootout winner to officially end Philadelphia’s postseason drought. Cam York’s seeing-eye wrist shot to vanquish the hated Pittsburgh Penguins . It was nice to have a hockey team in Philadelphia again. For a few months, if you could believe it, people were excited about the Flyers. The speed with which the club has traded dizzying highs for crushing lows has led to a different kind of hysteria. With the Flyers dead in the water amid a catastrophic start (7-11-6), the fanbase has propped up talented third-year winger Matvei Michkov as a franchise savior and painted anyone they perceive as a hindrance on his path to stardom, most notably coach Rick Tocchet, as a villain. For some fans, Tocchet’s frosty relationship with Michkov is a fireable offense in and of itself. The team is very bad, you see. Fowler won his first five road starts before losing 3-1 to the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden on Monday. At this pace, Fowler might win the Calder Trophy for the League's best rookie and the Vezina Trophy for best goalie. With the area that Paul’s stick hit, a wrist injury will also be a concern. items.body: NEWARK, N.J.— You could see it, right? The gaping hole in the Canadiens lineup left by one six-foot-three, 226-pound winger. If Monday’s loss was a harbinger of life without Josh Anderson , Montreal Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes might want to get on the line with his former agency and get the pending unrestricted free agent signed fast. After the game ended 3-1 New York Rangers, Martin St. Louis said the Canadiens were “flat,” that they had “no energy,” that they played “pretty much the worst hockey” they have all season, and he expressed hope it was a one-off. Are we going to get that level that Andy can bring? I don’t know. But we’re going to find out. It’s an opportunity for those guys, and I’m pretty sure their enthusiasm’s going to be pretty high. And during a time of normalcy, to get that injection from youth might not be a bad thing either. It’s an unfortunate situation, but it all depends on how you look at everything. items.title: Flames takeaways: Rookie Jonathan Castagna hits milestone in win
items.summary: Jonathan Castagna stole the show on Tuesday with his first two NHL goals, which were key to the Flames’ second win in three California road games.
items.body: On any other night, stripping Macklin Celebrini from a pretty good scoring opportunity would have been a highlight for Jonathan Castagna . But it paled in comparison to the fact he finished the night with the first two goals of his NHL career. “I’m really grateful for the opportunity in the first place,” the rookie centre told Sportsnet’s Brendan Parker following the Flames’ 5-2 win in San Jose. “To score a goal in this league is a really special moment. It’s been a long time coming. There have been a lot of chances I wish I could have back.” Castagna, who was acquired last season in the MacKenzie Weegar deal, was called up early from the Wranglers this season and has made it clear with his 200-foot game he isn’t going back. He extended the Flames lead to 4-1 early in the third when he fought his way to the front of the net and turned to bat in an Aydar Suniev rebound out of the air to kickstart a celebration that saw his teammates shower him with water as he did his fly-by. “They were spraying me with water pretty good — I was trying not to smile, and keep it cool, but it was a pretty special moment and I was smiling ear-to-ear,” said the Toronto native. “It’s really nice to finally get one in the back of the net, but also see the reaction from the guys being like that — it’s heartwarming.” With the net empty, and things getting chippy, Castagna batted in another one after Martin Pospisil did his best to ensure he got the puck to the popular young centre who swept it in. On a night when Pospisil and Matt Coronato scored to put the Flames up 2-1 in the first period, it was Castagna and another Flame who stole the show with milestone moments that were key to the team’s second win in three California road games. items.title: Gauthier ‘just flowing’ during 10-game goal streak for Ducks
items.summary: ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines.
items.body: Forward closing in on Selanne after fourth hat trick of season in loss to Blues ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines. So, the Anaheim Ducks forward is doing his best to adopt tunnel vision as he continues to score goals at a record pace. That was evident again on Tuesday, when he extended his goal streak to 10 games by getting a hat trick, his fourth during the run, in an 8-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues at Enterprise Center. ANA@STL: Gauthier records his fourth hat trick of the season and fifth of his career The 22-year-old, who also had an assist in the loss, has 19 goals during the streak, which is one game shy of tying Teemu Selanne (Oct. 21 to Nov. 10, 1997) for the longest in Ducks history. He's also the third player in NHL history to have a goal streak of at least 10 games before the age of 23, joining Babe Dye (11 games in 1920-21) and Mike Bossy (10 games in 1978-79). "It obviously gets published a lot what’s going on, but if I let the online chats and stuff, the pressure and all that stuff, get to me, it’s not going to be good," Gauthier told NHL.com. "When I play at my best, I’m playing free. I’m not thinking, I’m just flowing, I’m using my instincts and being great. I don’t let that affect me. I haven’t these last handful of weeks, so I’m going to keep that going." Gauthier certainly hasn't let it affect him, considering he has 24 points (19 goals, five assists) during an NHL career-high 12-game point streak. He also has 21 goals in 21 games this season, which is tied with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers for the NHL lead. The Leafs found fresh ways to stunt their momentum, allowing Chicago to strike back 35 seconds and 12 seconds, respectively, after their second- and third-period comeback goals. And the head man inside those visitors' coaching quarters boarded a plane home more disappointed than usual. “I’m disappointed tonight,” Jim Hiller said. “I’m disappointed every night. items.body: Forward to see time defending Suzuki, type of responsibility captain welcomes NEWARK, N.J. -- Nico Hischier knows his most important contribution for the New Jersey Devils won't always appear on the score sheet. That might be winning a defensive-zone face-off, staying above the puck instead of joining the rush or sacrificing an offensive opportunity to remain on the proper side of an opposing star. Those details will again be critical when the Devils host the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center for NHL on Prime "Wednesday Night Hockey" (7:30 p.m. ET; MSGSN, Prime). The Devils captain likely will spend significant time against Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki , who has 17 points (eight goals, nine assists) in 15 games while winning 55.4 percent of his face-offs. Suzuki's intelligence, patience with the puck and chemistry with Cole Caufield , who leads Montreal with 12 goals in 21 games, will test Hischier's positioning and awareness. "I view it as part of my game I want to play, and I take that as my job that game, and it contributes to the team," Hischier said. "I obviously take pride in that. If you're able to shut down a good line, then you give your team a chance to win a hockey game." Those assignments, combined with Hischier's production on offense and leadership as captain, have earned him respect throughout the NHL and inside New Jersey's dressing room. "He goes about the game and his business the right way," linemate Luke Evangelista said. "He's an honest player, works his hardest every night, plays a responsible 200-foot game. items.body: ST. PAUL, Minn. — Matt Boldy had two goals and an assist, and the Minnesota Wild scored six goals in the first 23 minutes as they cruised to their fourth straight victory, 7-3 over the Nashville Predators on Tuesday night. Brock Faber, Blake Coleman, Maxim Shabanov, Marcus Foligno and Joel Eriksson Ek also scored for the Central Division-leading Wild (16-3-4), who haven't lost in regulation since Oct. 22 at Calgary, a span of 12 games. Kirill Kaprizov had three assists to reach 40 points on the season. Nicolas Hague, Jonathan Marchessault and Filip Forsberg scored for the Predators (11-6-5), who have lost their last two after a seven-game win streak. Nashville's Justus Annunen was pulled early in the second period after allowing six goals on 20 shots, replaced by top goaltender Juuse Saros, who stopped 17 of 18 shots. Jesper Wallstedt had an easier night, making 25 saves for Minnesota. It was the highest-scoring game of the season for the Wild, who have 18 goals over their past three games. Shabanov and Boldy scored 43 seconds apart late in the first period to make it 4-0. Boldy scored again 59 seconds into the second period on the power play. Hague got the Predators on the board 53 seconds later, but Foligno made it 6-1 17 seconds after that. Nick Foligno had the assist on his younger brother's first goal of the season. Eriksson Ek capped the scoring with five seconds left in the second.
